svg.text: FIG 01: LINEARITY AXIOMS, SUPERPOSITION THEOREM & POWER NON-SUPERPOSITION ENGINE
Homogeneity & Additivity Criteria • Source Deactivation Rules • Dependent Source Invariance • Multi-Source Power Bounds & Frequency Orthogonality

g.text: 1. Linearity Axioms & Principles
The Two Fundamental Axioms of Linearity
• A system f(x) is linear if and only if it satisfies both:
1. Homogeneity: f(k · x) = k · f(x) (Scaling)
2. Additivity: f(x₁ + x₂) = f(x₁) + f(x₂) (Superposition)
• Combined Master Criterion: f(a · x₁ + b · x₂) = a · f(x₁) + b · f(x₂)
Strict Circuit Taxonomy:
✓ Linear Elements: Resistors (V=IR), Inductors (v=L di/dt), Capacitors (i=C dv/dt)
✓ Linear Sources: All 4 linear dependent sources (VCVS, VCCS, CCVS, CCCS)
✗ Non-Linear Elements: Diodes (Shockley exponential), Transistors (large signal),
Varactors, saturable inductors, squaring elements, and non-linear loads
The Affine Function Trap: y = mx + c (c ≠ 0)
• Graphically: A straight line not passing through origin (0, 0).
• Testing Homogeneity: f(kx) = m(kx) + c ≠ k(mx + c) = k·f(x)!
• Testing Additivity: f(x₁+x₂) = m(x₁+x₂) + c ≠ (mx₁+c) + (mx₂+c) = mx₁+mx₂+2c!
Exam Golden Rule: y = mx + c is an AFFINE SYSTEM, NOT LINEAR!
• Only incremental response Δy = m Δx is linear. Circuit with independent internal
sources exhibits affine response V_out = m · V_in + V_th (c = V_th ≠ 0).
Homogeneity Method for Ladder Networks
When finding input-output transfer ratio in passive resistor ladders:
1. Assume load output current I_out = 1 A (or V_out = 1 V).
2. Work backwards across the ladder calculating all node voltages & currents.
3. Arrive at input source excitation: V_in,assumed = V_calc.
4. Scale factor k = V_in,actual / V_in,assumed.
5. True response: I_out,actual = k · 1 A.
Benefit: Solves complex 5-loop ladders in 45 seconds without simultaneous equations!
Critical Boundaries: When Linearity Fails
1. Power Response: P = I²R or V²/R is quadratic (Degree 2) → Superposition FAILS.
2. Semiconductor Diodes: i = I_s(e^{v/ηV_T} - 1) is non-linear.
3. Magnetic Saturation: B-H hysteresis curve non-linearity.
4. Time-Varying Systems: R(t), L(t), C(t) require parametric analysis.
5. Circuits with Initial Stored Energy: Inductor i_L(0⁻) ≠ 0 or Capacitor v_C(0⁻) ≠ 0
must be converted to equivalent independent sources before applying linearity!
Core Takeaway for GATE 2027:
Linearity guarantees uniqueness and scalability of solutions for voltages and currents.
2. Source Deactivation (Killing) Mechanics
Deactivation Axioms for Independent Sources
Ideal Independent Voltage Source (V_s):
• Deactivated by setting terminal potential difference to zero: V_s = 0 V.
→ REPLACE WITH SHORT CIRCUIT (Zero Resistance: R_in = 0 Ω)
Ideal Independent Current Source (I_s):
• Deactivated by setting branch throughput current to zero: I_s = 0 A.
→ REPLACE WITH OPEN CIRCUIT (Infinite Resistance: R_in = ∞ Ω)
Practical sources: Retain internal series resistor R_se or shunt resistor R_sh!
THE TITAN LAW: NEVER KILL A DEPENDENT SOURCE!
Controlled sources (VCVS, VCCS, CCVS, CCCS) are NOT independent excitations.
They represent internal coupling elements controlled by circuit variables (Vx, Ix).
Why Killing Controlled Sources Causes Fatal Errors:
1. Deactivating a dependent source changes the fundamental topology of the circuit.
2. It severs the physical feedback loop between control branch and active element.
3. It yields completely erroneous Thevenin resistance R_th and Superposition results.
RULE: Dependent sources remain FULLY ACTIVE in EVERY sub-circuit!
In each sub-problem, their control variables take NEW local values (Vx', Vx'').
Source Transformation Equivalence & Boundaries
Thévenin branch (V_s in series with R_s) ↔ Norton branch (I_s in parallel with R_s):
V_s = I_s · R_s ⟺ I_s = V_s / R_s (R_series = R_parallel = R_s)
The 3 Fatal Traps of Source Transformation:
1. Never absorb or transform a branch that contains the CONTROLLING VARIABLE (Vx, Ix)!
If the controlling branch is merged, the control variable is lost forever.
2. Never transform a branch where the target response is to be measured!
3. Internal power dissipation is NOT conserved across source transformations:
P_int(Thévenin) = (I_L)² · R_s ≠ P_int(Norton) = (I_s - I_L)² · R_s
Transformation guarantees external terminal equivalence ONLY, not internal power!
Redundant Elements Axioms
1. Resistor in Parallel with Ideal Voltage Source:
• Terminal voltage is rigidly clamped to V_s regardless of R_p.
• R_p can be REMOVED (opened) when calculating voltages/currents in rest of network.
• (Caution: R_p draws power V_s²/R_p directly from source; affects total source power).
2. Resistor in Series with Ideal Current Source:
• Branch current is rigidly fixed to I_s regardless of R_s.
• R_s can be SHORTED when calculating voltages/currents in rest of network.
• (Caution: R_s drops voltage I_s·R_s; alters total voltage across the current source).
Exam Shortcut: Eliminating redundant branches simplifies nodes by 50%!
3. Superposition Theorem Algorithm
Formal Statement & Mathematical Formulation
In any linear, bilateral, time-invariant electric network containing N independent sources,
the response (branch voltage or current) equals the algebraic sum of the individual
responses produced by each independent source acting alone.
y_total = ∑_{k=1}^N y_k = y₁ + y₂ + ... + y_N
Linear Matrix Form: y = [a₁ a₂ ... a_N] · [S₁ S₂ ... S_N]ᵀ
where a_k are constant transfer coefficients determined purely by network resistances.
The 4-Step Standard Superposition Algorithm
Step 1: Identify all Independent Sources (S₁, S₂, ..., S_N)
• Number of sub-circuits equals total number of independent sources N.
Step 2: Isolate Source S_k (Sub-Circuit k)
• Keep source S_k active.
• Deactivate all other independent voltage sources (short circuit).
• Deactivate all other independent current sources (open circuit).
• Keep ALL dependent sources intact and active!
Step 3: Solve Sub-Circuit k for Target Response y_k
• Write KCL/KVL to determine y_k with strict regard to reference polarity.
Step 4: Algebraic Superposition
y_net = y₁ + y₂ + ... + y_N (respecting +/- signs!)
Solving Dependent Source Circuits via Superposition
Consider circuit with 50 V source, 2 A source, and 3Ix dependent source:
Sub-circuit 1 (50 V active, 2 A open):
Controlling current: Ix' = 50 / (R₁ + R₂ + 3) = 2.5 A
Target voltage: V₁ = Ix' · R_L = 20 V
Sub-circuit 2 (2 A active, 50 V short):
Controlling current: Ix'' = -1.2 A (due to 2 A injection)
Target voltage: V₂ = Ix'' · R_L = -9.6 V
Net Response:
V_total = V₁ + V₂ = 20 V + (-9.6 V) = +10.4 V
Efficiency Audit: When NOT to Use Superposition
• If a circuit has 4 independent sources, Superposition requires solving 4 sub-circuits!
• Systematic Nodal Analysis requires only 1 matrix solution: [Y][V] = [I].
GATE Decision Rule:
1. If independent sources N ≥ 3 → PREFER NODAL ANALYSIS (Saves 60% exam time!).
2. Use Superposition when:
- Question asks for contribution of a specific source alone.
- Network contains orthogonal frequencies (DC + AC, or ω₁ ≠ ω₂).
- Deactivating one source causes circuit to collapse into simple series-parallel.
Strategic insight wins top ranks: match tool to problem topology!
4. Power Non-Superposition & Orthogonality
THE FATAL FALLACY: P_total ≠ P₁ + P₂
Power is a quadratic function of current or voltage: P = i² · R.
Because squaring is non-linear ((a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab ≠ a² + b²):
P_total = (i₁ ± i₂)² · R = i₁²R + i₂²R ± 2 i₁ i₂ R
P_total = P₁ + P₂ ± 2√(P₁ · P₂) (Cross-Product Term!)
The cross-product term ±2√(P₁P₂) represents non-linear interaction.
Power adds algebraically IF AND ONLY IF the cross-product integrates to zero!
Multi-Source DC Power Bounds Matrix
When source polarities or current directions in resistor R are unconstrained:
Maximum Possible Power (Constructive Addition):
P_max = (√P₁ + √P₂)² [General: P_max = (∑ √P_k)²]
Minimum Possible Power (Destructive Cancellation):
P_min = (√P₁ - √P₂)² [General: P_min = |∑ ±√P_k|_min²]
Classroom Drill: P₁ = 18 W alone, P₂ = 8 W alone in same resistor R:
The Orthogonal Frequency Exception
When can we legally add powers? WHEN SOURCES ARE MUTUALLY ORTHOGONAL!
Orthogonality condition over common fundamental period T:
⟨i₁, i₂⟩ = (1/T) ∫₀ᵀ i₁(t) · i₂(t) dt ≡ 0
Orthogonal Excitation Regimes where P_avg = ∑ P_k:
1. DC Source + AC Source: ∫₀ᵀ I_dc · I_m cos(ωt + θ) dt = 0
P_total = P_dc + P_ac = (I_dc)²R + (I_rms)²R
2. Distinct Harmonic Frequencies: ω₁ ≠ ω₂
P_avg = ∑_{k=1}^M (I_k,rms)² · R
DANGER: If ω₁ = ω₂, orthogonality FAILS due to cross phase cos(θ₁ - θ₂)!
